note: Adapted from entry No. 40 of Hagen 1858, 'Monographie der Termiten'; the original is in Latin (Walker's original description) plus German (Hagen's translation). Hagen states that he gives no separate detailed description and only translates Walker's original, so the content of this section is in fact Walker's original description; only the alate (imago) is known, and the author notes that it belongs to Eutermes and is closest in form and colour to T. opacus. At the end another worker, doubtfully of this species, 'Nasutus', is recorded from Elmeo Island (collected on the circumnavigation of the Swedish frigate Eugenie, in the Stockholm museum), body length 3 mm, form and colour almost identical with the T. corniger described under T. morio; whether it is the same species is doubtful, and it is not merged into this section.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Belongs to the Eutermes group, closest in form and colour to T. opacus. Whole body pitch black, hairy, shining, the body almost linear, the venter leather-yellow; head almost elliptical, far longer than wide, the vertex depressed, the anterior part leather-yellow, as wide as the thorax; ocelli close to the compound eyes; mandible tips black; antennae leather-yellow, slightly longer than the head, the segments nearly equal; pronotum almost twice as wide as long, anterior margin concave, posterior margin convex, sides slightly convex; abdomen club-shaped, yellow beneath, slightly longer and wider than the thorax; legs leather-yellow, tibiae darker than the femora; tarsal segment 4 almost twice as long as the preceding segments; wings brown, more than twice as long as the body, veins brown, marginal cell without cross-veins, numerous indistinct cross-veins between the subcosta and the media, media forked, submedia with 12 branches.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Original Latin description (Walker's text, translated by Hagen): Piceus, subtus, antennis pedibusque fulvis; caput antice fulvum; abdomen subtus luteum, alae fuscae. Measurements: body length 5 mm (2 lignes); wingspan 24 mm (12 lignes). For the German rendering see the items under Diagnostic characters. Locality: New Holland (Neuholland), in the British Museum.
